inputs.original_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to finish renegotiating the 2009 agreement or face an indefinite nationwide strike. The fact that workers must threaten to withdraw their labor just to get long-unresolved commitments taken seriously shows the imbalance: universities rely on non-teaching staff, while their work and livelihoods are treated as expendable. This is not a failure of workers to be patient; it is a failure of institutions to honor their obligations. The government should negotiate seriously and deliver fair treatment before workers are forced to shut things down.
inputs.modified_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to complete renegotiations of the 2009 agreement, or face an indefinite nationwide strike. Workers should not have to threaten disruption to make institutions honor their commitments—but when dialogue is ignored, collective action may be the only leverage they have. Universities depend on non-teaching staff, and treating their work and livelihoods as expendable is part of a broader failure to respect labor. The government needs to negotiate seriously and deliver fair treatment, rather than leave workers to bear the cost of its inaction.
